applies_why: The judge text decides a D6-vs-C1 collision between the challenger's seed/loins chain and the defender's chain, which is the chain-against-chain setting K-C governs.
quote: the challenger's seed/loins chain is footed but does not name Joseph as the begetter; the defender's chain is footed but rests on the woman-route inference.
rule_words: the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: "never verse by verse": two readings are (1) it bars faulting a chain for not explicitly naming Joseph, which the judge did; (2) it only bars isolated-verse weighing, leaving chain-level inference judgments allowed.
why: The judge faults the challenger's chain for not naming Joseph as begetter, which is an explicit-naming/stating-verse test rather than chain-footing comparison, so it breaches K-C.
